newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Lower sales hurt Brazil's Brahma '96 net.
newsitem.headline: Lower sales hurt Brazil's Brahma '96 net.

text.p: Latin America's largest brewer Brahma said its modest 1996 results were hurt by low sales growth which was not sufficient to cover new investment costs.
"The company bore all the costs of the expansion without a corresponding increase in revenue," the company's board said in a statement.
Earlier today, Brahma reported a 1996 net profit of 324.9 million reais under Corporate Law accounting, an increase of 23.2 percent over 1995.
Under the inflation-adjusted accounting method, Brahma's net profit totalled 371.3 million reais, up 35.9 percent from 1995, the company said in a statement.
The company has reported it would pay dividends of 10.90 reais per 1,000 shares.
The company said poor weather last year, which saw either rain or cool temperatures on 60 percent of weekends, cut into beer sales.
In Brazil, the volume of Brahma's beer sales rose only 2.83 percent to 36.3 million hectolitres last year. Net sales revenues rose only 0.92 percent to 2.468 billion reais in 1996, the firm said.
The cost of goods sold last year rose 8.9 percent in 1996 while the total unit volume sold rose just 7.2 percent, the company said.

Cost increases were attributed mainly to the start-up of the Nova Rio plant, the largest plant in Latin America with a production capacity of 13.8 million hectolitres of beer and five million hectolitres of soft drinks a year.
By the end of this year, the Nova Rio plant will account for 36 percent of Brahma's total output.
The company said investments made last year would not begin to bear fruit until this year.
Moreover, Brahma expects the market to resume its trend of stronger growth in the next few years, which would allow the firm to bring its growth rates to historical levels.
